supplement.where: Appendices A-C, PDF pp. 18-30. The preregistration link is https://osf.io/3u8tq/overview?view_only=e1a8044dd5044bc59dd0a7d8f3fca3c2 (p. 3, footnote 2). No separate supplementary document is identified.
supplement.holds: Appendix A supplies interface, recruitment, exclusion, model-setting and actual-payment details; Appendix B explains AI-text adoption measures; Appendix C contains numeric diversity differences and significance stars in Table 5 (p. 28), adoption-stratified differences in Table 6 (p. 30), and supplementary figures. No numerical SEs or confidence intervals for the diversity effects are printed. Tables 2 and 4 do print demographic SEs.

paper_design_summary: One online experiment block-randomized Prolific participants to AI assistance versus writing alone, crossed with originality versus technical-quality incentives (pp. 3-4). Participants wrote short stories; computed measures compared diversity across final stories and in-progress drafts, while individual creativity and quality were not scored (pp. 6-9, 14, 25). The paper reports 200 recruited people and 50 per cell, but exact randomized and analyzed totals are unconfirmed after the reported 29 exclusions; disjoint high- and low-adoption groups establish at least 64 analyzed people (27 + 37) in this experiment (pp. 3, 5, 11, 13, 25, 28, 30).

studies.label: 2x2 online experiment: AI access x incentive (short story writing)

assignment.what_was_assigned: AI writing assistant access (AI vs SELF) crossed with bonus incentive (originality O vs technical quality T)
assignment.quote: We run a pre-registered, between-subjects experiment in which participants are assigned via block randomization to one of four conditions
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 3, footnote 2 (OSF link); p. 5, Section 4 states that its analyses were preregistered except Figure 1 (right); p. 8, Section 5 and p. 9, Section 6 identify subsequent analyses as exploratory.

arms.name: AI-O
arms.description: Integrated GPT5-mini chat assistant available during writing. Announced originality/uniqueness competition: top 2% $7, top 2-10% $4, top 10-25% $2 (p. 19, Figure 8). The actual post-study bonus was a fixed $1 for every completed work (p. 25, Appendix A.4).

arms.name: SELF-O
arms.description: Writing alone in a text editor; external AI forbidden. Announced originality/uniqueness competition: top 2% $7, top 2-10% $4, top 10-25% $2 (p. 19, Figure 8). The actual post-study bonus was a fixed $1 for every completed work (p. 25, Appendix A.4).

arms.name: AI-T
arms.description: Integrated GPT5-mini chat assistant available during writing. Announced organization/technique rubric: A $2.50, B $1.00; creativity explicitly excluded from grading (p. 19, Figure 8). The actual post-study bonus was a fixed $1 for every completed work (p. 25, Appendix A.4).

arms.name: SELF-T
arms.description: Writing alone in a text editor; external AI forbidden. Announced organization/technique rubric: A $2.50, B $1.00; creativity explicitly excluded from grading (p. 19, Figure 8). The actual post-study bonus was a fixed $1 for every completed work (p. 25, Appendix A.4).

participants.exclusions: Appendix A.2 reports 29 Prolific workers filtered out and describes one SELF participant excluded after a post-hoc writing-pattern check; that participant was paid, and their incentive arm is not stated (p. 25). Safeguards terminated sessions after 5 full-screen/window violations or 6 inactivity warnings; instruction and prompt attention-check failures also ended participation (pp. 20, 25, Appendix A.2). Section 3.1 reports 200 recruited people and 50 per group, and Table 2 reports 50 per demographic group (pp. 3, 5). The PDF does not explicitly reconcile those counts with all exclusions or describe replacement recruitment, so neither the total nor per-arm exact analyzed counts are confirmed; exact randomized counts and stage-specific/arm-specific exclusion counts also remain unconfirmed. No addition or subtraction of the exclusions is treated as an observed denominator. The 11 submissions outside the word limit were retained in the final analysis (p. 20, Appendix A.1.4). Separately, Table 4 reports 27 high-adoption and 37 low-adoption participants (p. 13), defined as A > 0.8 and A < 0.2 (p. 28, Appendix C.3) and analyzed on their final submissions (p. 11, Section 6.2; p. 30, Table 6). These mutually exclusive groups establish a lower bound of 27 + 37 = 64 analyzed people in the same experiment; 64 is a derived lower bound, not the exact full-sample denominator.
participants.who: Prolific workers aged at least 18, residing in the US or UK, with English as their primary language or fluent English, at least 500 completed Prolific tasks and at least 98% approval (p. 25, Appendix A.3). Table 2 (p. 5) reports student proportions of 0.14, 0.22, 0.21 and 0.11, and mean ages of 40.74, 39.86, 41.32 and 40.04, in AI-O, SELF-O, AI-T, SELF-T order.
participants.quote: 200 participants from Prolific, with 50 participants per group.
participants.locator: p. 3, Section 3.1 (quoted recruitment count, not a confirmed analyzed count); p. 5, Table 2 and caption (reported demographic groups); pp. 20, 25, Appendix A.2 (unreconciled exclusions); p. 25, Appendix A.3 (recruitment criteria); p. 13, Table 4 (27 high-adoption and 37 low-adoption participants); p. 28, Appendix C.3 (disjoint thresholds); p. 11, Section 6.2 and p. 30, Table 6 (final-submission analyses of these groups).

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT5-mini; Appendix A.1.4 spells the model gpt5-mini and sets reasoning to medium (p. 1; p. 20).
ai_tool.how_used: An integrated chat panel beside the editor was available during writing, but not the initial brainstorming phase. Participants had to prompt it at least once, could use up to 15 calls/prompts, and could copy-paste within the study window (p. 4, Section 3.2.1; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4; p. 25, Appendix A.2). The paper reports 3.57 conversation turns on average and 91% requesting a full draft at least once; requests were editing 38%, drafting 30%, creative consulting 14%, mechanical assistance 3%, and other 15% (p. 5, AI Usage).

task.description: Write a 250-350 word first-person short story taking place over no more than one day and centered on a decision or dilemma, after outlining Main Character, Setting, Conflict, Resolution and Plot (p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 20, Appendix A.1.3).
task.duration: Brainstorming: minimum 1 minute and maximum 5 minutes, without AI. Writing: minimum 5 minutes and maximum 20 minutes; an additional 5-minute grace period applied if outside the word limit. Average study duration was 25 minutes (p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4).

outcomes.name: Embedding similarity of final stories within each randomized cell
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Participant-level leave-one-out mean cosine similarity to other final stories in the same cell, using the prespecified suite all-MiniLM-L12-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, embeddinggemma-300m, Style-Embedding, STAR and byt5 (p. 6, Section 4.1.1 and Table 3). These are robustness views of the same diversity outcome, combined here rather than separate outcomes. Diversity is the paper's primary outcome (p. 14, Section 7.2); Section 4 analyses were preregistered (p. 5), but no individual embedding model is designated the sole preregistered primary. Section 5 features all-MiniLM-L12-v2 (p. 8). AI was available in AI-O/AI-T and absent in SELF-O/SELF-T; mixed refers to those arms, not removal of AI after exposure. Adoption-stratified estimates in Table 6 are exploratory robustness analyses on post-treatment subsets, not separate randomized experiments.

MiniLM and most models indicate lower diversity with AI; signs are mixed across the full suite. MiniLM, mpnet, embeddinggemma and star also have BH ***; byt5 has no BH star. Text-reported MiniLM means: AI-O final 0.26; SELF-O 0.22.

diversity_detail.metric: For participant i in cell g: Y_i = sum over j in g, j != i, of cosine similarity between story embeddings, divided by (n_g - 1); contrasts compare these participant-level scores across cells (p. 6, Section 4.1.1).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L12-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, embeddinggemma-300m, Style-Embedding (Wegmann et al.), STAR, byt5
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each final story against all other final stories in the same randomized cell (p. 6, Section 4.1.1). Exact analyzed cell denominators are unconfirmed: Table 2 reports 50 people per demographic group, but does not reconcile those counts with the reported exclusions (p. 5, Table 2; p. 25, Appendix A.2).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: One-sided two-sample Welch t-tests on participant-level leave-one-out scores (pp. 6-7). Table 5 gives ordinary black and BH-adjusted red stars: * p < 0.1, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01. No numerical SE, CI or exact p-value is supplied for these diversity effects. Shared story pairs make the scores dependent; no correction for this dependence is described.
diversity_detail.notes: Printed positive similarity differences mean lower diversity in the first-named group; no standardized effect was computed. Table 6 (p. 30), MiniLM exploratory adoption subsets: AI-O - SELF-O low 0.015, high 0.069***; AI-T - SELF-T low 0.051***, high 0.072***; AI-T - AI-O low 0.041**, high 0.008. Low adoption is A < 0.2 and high adoption A > 0.8 (p. 28, Appendix C.3); Table 4 (p. 13) gives 37 low- and 27 high-adoption people across AI arms, not per contrast. Table 6 significance markings conflict with Figure 6 in places, including all-mpnet-base AI-T - SELF-T, low adoption: 0.021 without a star in the table, but a star in the figure (pp. 12, 30); retain the printed table values without reconciling exact p-values.

outcomes.name: N-gram/token-based similarity and diversity of final stories within cell
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Compression ratio, self-BLEU, ROUGE-L, and n-gram diversity scores with n = 2 and n = 3 (p. 6, Table 3; p. 28, Table 5). The first three measure similarity; higher NGDS means greater diversity. These are the prespecified lexical/token views of diversity, grouped as one outcome. Section 4 analyses were preregistered (p. 5); no individual lexical metric is declared the sole primary. AI was available while AI-arm stories were produced and absent in SELF arms. The general participant-level leave-one-out definition is given, but metric-specific pairwise implementations for compression ratio and NGDS are not described.

contrasts.reported: Table 5, Final, AI-O - SELF-O: compression ratio -0.083; self bleu -0.001; rougel -0.003; n gram diversity score 2 0.095; n gram diversity score 3 0.103. No stars are printed. NGDS entries retain the diversity scale; Figure 1 reverses their signs for presentation alongside similarity metrics.

diversity_detail.metric: Compression ratio, self-BLEU, ROUGE-L and NGDS; Table 3 defines NGDS using unique/all n-gram counts, and Table 5 reports n = 2 and n = 3.
diversity_detail.computed_over: The paper defines a participant-level leave-one-out comparison within each cell. How compression ratio and NGDS are converted into pairwise S(X_i, X_j) functions is not specified (p. 6, Section 4.1.1).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: One-sided Welch tests; Table 5 reports significance through stars and none appear for these Final entries. This concerns the paper's directional hypotheses and is not a two-sided equivalence test. Numerical SEs and exact p-values are not printed.
diversity_detail.notes: Table 5 reports NGDS in its original diversity direction; its positive AI-minus-SELF final values are consistent with Figure 15, whereas Figure 1 explicitly flips NGDS and displays negative values. No numerical effect or sign reversal has been computed in this form.

outcomes.name: Embedding similarity of in-progress drafts over session time (30-second snapshots)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Exploratory participant-draft trajectories: the same within-cell similarity construction at 30-second intervals, restricted to text of at least 200 words; final submissions are carried forward after a participant finishes. Main text and Figure 2(b) use all-MiniLM-L12-v2; Figure 16 supplies the other embedding and lexical metrics as robustness views (pp. 8-9, Section 5; p. 29, Figure 16). Retained separately because these are in-progress outputs rather than only final stories.

contrasts.reported: The text says AI-O and AI-T collectively increase diversity after 5 minutes into the session and begin to diverge around 12 minutes after. Figure 2(b) shows the subsequent AI-O trajectory as less similar than AI-T. No numerical between-arm trajectory effect, SE or interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Figure 2(b) and text; p. 29, Figure 16

diversity_detail.metric: Leave-one-out mean cosine similarity within cell at each 30-second snapshot
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L12-v2 in main text; all Table 3 metrics in Figure 16
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each participant's snapshot against the other participants' snapshots in the same cell at the same time point
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Shaded bands appear in the plots; their construction and level are not stated (p. 9, Figure 2(b); p. 29, Figure 16).

outcomes.name: Context: diversity of first full AI-generated drafts versus final submissions
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Exploratory analysis of the first valid full draft generated by the assistant for participants who requested one, using the same embedding suite (lexical variants are also displayed). Retained because the source supports this analysis, but question is none and scored_on_output is false for the criterion about participant-produced outputs: these observations score assistant-generated drafts. Section 4 explicitly excludes Figure 1 (right) from preregistered analyses (p. 5).

contrasts.reported: Section 5.2 text reports MiniLM similarity 0.39 for AI-O first drafts and 0.26 for AI-O final submissions; SELF-O baseline is 0.22. Section 4.2 states that first AI drafts were on average 45% more similar across all metrics than AI-assisted final submissions. These are printed descriptions, not an effect calculated here; no unambiguous numerical inferential estimate is assigned to this first-versus-final contrast.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Section 4.2 Hypothesis 1 and Section 5.2; p. 9, continuation of Section 5.2 and Figure 2(a)

diversity_detail.metric: Within-cell leave-one-out cosine similarity, with other Table 3 metrics as robustness views.
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L12-v2 featured; full embedding suite in Table 5 and Figure 15.
diversity_detail.computed_over: First full AI-generated drafts within AI conditions, compared descriptively with final participant submissions. Exact group/sample definition for Table 5 First (AI) contrasts is unclear.

diversity_detail.notes: Table 5 (p. 28), all-MiniLM-L12, First (AI), prints 0.212*** under AI-O - SELF-O, 0.191*** under AI-T - SELF-T, and -0.017 under AI (T - O). The first two also have BH ***. In contrast, Figure 1 (right) and Section 4.2 (p. 7) describe first AI draft minus final submission within AI arms. These values cannot safely be mapped to a single comparator from the PDF alone. The same ambiguous table columns include compression ratio 0.087*** and self bleu 0.022*** under AI-O - SELF-O; they are preserved only as labeled source values.

company_involvement.description: No company funding, data contribution or authorship is stated. Both authors are affiliated with MIT; OpenAI supplies the model used in the experiment. This is absence of a reported company research role, not proof that no involvement occurred.

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1 is met: individual block randomization crossed AI access with originality versus technical-quality incentives (p. 3, Section 3; p. 4, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2). Criterion 2 is met without assuming that 200 or 50 per arm are exact analyzed counts: Table 4 reports 27 high-adoption and 37 low-adoption people (p. 13); Appendix C.3 defines disjoint groups, A > 0.8 and A < 0.2 (p. 28), whose final submissions are analyzed in Section 6.2 and Table 6 (pp. 11, 30). Their sum, 27 + 37 = 64, is a conservative lower bound on distinct analyzed people in this single experiment, not an additional study or an exact total. The reported recruitment/demographic counts of 200 and 50 per group are not explicitly reconciled with 29 exclusions, so exact randomized and analyzed totals and per-arm counts remain null (pp. 3, 5, 20, 25). Criterion 3 is met: computed within-cell similarity/diversity scores assess participants' produced stories (p. 6, Section 4.1.1; p. 7, Section 4.2). The assistant was available during writing in AI arms (p. 20, Appendix A.1.4); final-story and in-progress diversity outcomes answer across_people. No AI-removal outcome is reported. Incentive-only contrasts use other because the AI configuration did not change.

one_line_finding: AI increased final-story MiniLM similarity by 0.043 under originality incentives and 0.062 under technical-quality incentives (both p < 0.01); originality incentives reduced similarity among AI users by 0.023 (p < 0.05), with variation across embedding models (p. 28, Table 5).
open_questions: The reported 200 recruited people and Table 2 groups of 50 are not explicitly reconciled with 29 exclusions, including a described post-hoc SELF exclusion; exact randomized and analyzed totals, arm-specific exclusions, and any replacement recruitment remain unconfirmed (pp. 3, 5, 20, 25). This does not leave criterion 2 open: the disjoint groups of 27 high-adoption and 37 low-adoption participants establish at least 64 analyzed people (pp. 11, 13, 28, 30).
The exact AI-T final-story MiniLM mean is plotted but not numerically printed; participant-level scores or a numerical arm summary are needed (p. 9, Figure 2(a)).
Metric-specific pairwise implementations of compression ratio and NGDS are not supplied despite the general participant-level formula (p. 6).

Table 5 First (AI) column headers conflict with Figure 1 (right) and the accompanying description of a first-draft-minus-final comparison; the numerical estimates cannot be assigned confidently to comparators (pp. 7-9, 28).

Figure 6 and Table 6 disagree on significance markings for some adoption-stratified effects, including the low-adoption mpnet AI-T - SELF-T result; corrected p-values or analysis output are needed (pp. 12, 30).

The scope of the statement that extra prompting effort does not yield significant AI-O versus AI-T diversity changes is unclear relative to the aggregate and adoption-stratified tables (p. 11, Section 6.2; pp. 28, 30, Tables 5-6).
Diversity-effect SEs, exact p-values, and the definition of plotted error bars/bands are not supplied; underlying scores or author clarification would be required for uncertainty extraction.
notes: The entire markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A-C, was read. Relevant passages and every retained numerical statistic were checked against PDF text/tables; raster figures were also inspected in memory where necessary, without creating files. The source is the saved arXiv v1; candidate-record claims about other versions were not treated as verified facts. Seven embedding models are one final-story outcome, with the lexical suite separate; exploratory trajectories and first-AI-draft context are retained. Preregistered_primary refers to the diversity suite, not a uniquely nominated metric. Similarity directions in contrasts are expressed as diversity directions; where component metrics have opposite signs, direction is mixed. Post-treatment adoption subsets are robustness/context analyses and must not be treated as independently randomized samples. AI-text adoption itself, prompting activity, survey attitudes, and qualitative PCA plots are not separate eligible creativity/diversity outcomes. There is no stated sample overlap or public data/code URL. No effect size, SD or SE was calculated, no plotted numerical arm mean was estimated, and no inferential value was invented. Final review independently covered the full markdown and checked the relevant PDF passages, tables and figures. The people challenge is corrected: exact analyzed counts previously recorded as 200 overall and 50 per arm are now null, and every active prose claim treating them as analyzed denominators has been removed or qualified. Criterion 2 instead rests on the disjoint 27- and 37-person analyzed adoption groups; the only new count arithmetic is the transparent lower bound 27 + 37 = 64. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as audit history; its earlier 200/50 analyzed-count conclusions are superseded by this final correction. All seven open-question topics, including the five unresolved reconciliation differences, are addressed in final.open_items and none prevents a decision on the three eligibility criteria.
